title: Metrics and Monitoring
description: Learn to collect, visualize, and alert on metrics for microservices health and performance.

data.text: Metrics provide quantitative measurements of your microservices' health and performance. Google, Netflix, and Uber all rely on metrics dashboards and alerting to detect issues before users notice them.

data.title: Essential Microservices Metrics
items: Error rate: Percentage of failed requests
Latency: p50, p95, p99 response times
Saturation: CPU, memory, disk, network usage
Availability: Uptime percentage (often expressed as nines)

data.text: The most popular monitoring stack for microservices is Prometheus + Grafana. Prometheus scrapes metrics from services via HTTP endpoints. Grafana visualizes metrics in dashboards. Alertmanager handles alert routing and notifications.

data.title: RED Method
data.text: The RED method focuses on three key metrics per service: Rate (requests per second), Errors (failed requests), and Duration (latency). This simple framework ensures you monitor what matters most.

items.question: What is the difference between push and pull metrics?
items.answer: Prometheus uses pull: it scrapes metrics from services. Push-based systems like StatsD require services to send metrics. Pull is simpler for dynamic environments; push is better for batch jobs.

items.question: How long should I retain metrics?
items.answer: Retain detailed metrics for 15-30 days. Aggregate metrics can be retained for months or years. Choose based on your analysis needs and storage costs.

items.question: What about cloud monitoring?
items.answer: Cloud providers offer managed metrics: CloudWatch (AWS), Stackdriver (GCP), Azure Monitor. They integrate well with cloud services but may lack the flexibility of Prometheus + Grafana.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Focus on RED method metrics: Rate, Errors, Duration
Use Prometheus + Grafana for metrics collection and visualization
Alert on SLO violations, not just thresholds
Monitor golden signals from every service
data.takeaway: Metrics provide the quantitative foundation of observability; instrument all services thoroughly.
